predictions.title: Qatar-8 b: transit mid-times from November 2026 to May 2027
predictions.question: When will Qatar-8 b transit between 2026-11-15 and 2027-05-15 (BJD_TDB)?

ephemeris.prior_note: published ephemeris agrees with the new times (0.3 sigma) and is a prior
ephemeris.law: t(N) = t0 + N P, N counted from the published reference transit (N = 0)

heldout.reason: forecast 5 later transits 353 days ahead with chi-square 1.32 per transit

ephemeris.method: weighted least squares on TESS mid-times (errors scaled by their own scatter, never down) plus the published t0 and P as independent Gaussian prior rows when they agree within 3 sigma; intervals from the fit covariance (68%: 1 sigma, 95%: 1.96 sigma)

scoring.rule: a hit when an independently measured mid-time (new TESS sector or ExoClock/ETD amateur timing) lies inside the 95% window; reported per transit and as the share of hits. The window is widened in quadrature by the measurement's own 95% error (fixed now, before any measurement: an amateur timing good to 1 to 2 minutes cannot test a window of seconds); how many fall inside the window as registered is reported too. Transits nobody measured count as neither.
sources_to_check: TESS SPOC 2-min light curves of TIC 103751498 observed after registration (MAST, lightkurve; scripts/score_predictions.py)
ExoClock observations of Qatar-8 b: https://www.exoclock.space/database/planets
Exoplanet Transit Database (VarAstro) transits of Qatar-8: https://var.astro.cz/ETD

predictions.title: Fireball over Douglas County, Washington, 2026 August 14 07:48 UTC: where its meteorites landed, predicted blind
predictions.question: Where do recovered meteorites of each mass lie on the ground, if any are found?

prediction.frame: along/across the ground track from the end state (fireball_demo.along_cross)

scoring.rule: a hit when a recovered meteorite's reported find site lies inside the predicted 95% region of its mass bin (the bin nearest its reported mass); score after finds are published. Inside means fewer than 95% of that bin's stored landing points have a higher Gaussian kernel density (scipy gaussian_kde, default bandwidth, in metres along and across the track) than the find site (scripts/fireball_new.py score_find)
